# Invoice Admin Nav Taxonomy — Group 1 "Policy & Scope"

Corpus root: `/mnt/c/Users/manci/PROJECTS/concur-corpus/CONCUR_INVOICE/`
Shorthand below: `ADMIN/` = `concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/`, `TOOLS/` = `concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/`

## Headline finding: the missing middle node

**All three pages hang off an intermediate menu the URLs don't reveal: `Invoice Processing Admin`.** No page in Group 1 is reached directly from `Administration`. The 2026_08 docs render the same path two interchangeable ways — as a menu-name sequence, or as a breadcrumb with `(left menu)` appended to the leaf. They are the same click sequence; the bridging sentence is explicit:

> `Administrators can access the tool from the Invoice Processing Admin left menu to view, add, modify, or delete group configurations.`
> — `ADMIN/access-the-group-configurations-tool-6f974fe5.md`

**Zero hits** across all 1,859 files for `PolicyAdmin`, `groupConfiguration`, `invoiceSettings`, or `dcredirect`. The corpus never publishes an `.asp` URL. Click path is the only navigable knowledge that exists here.

## Naming drift and renames — explicit findings

**1. `Invoice Admin` is a live alias for the `Administration > Invoice` node.** Four topics collapse the path and skip `Invoice Processing Admin` entirely:
> `(Administration > Invoice Admin > Invoice Settings)`
> — `ADMIN/invoice-header-import-record-type-300-format-9505828e.md` (also `...-310-...-21975178.md`, `invoice-line-item-import-record-type-420-format-0880199e.md`)
> `1.  As the Invoice Tax Administrator, click Administration > Invoice Admin > Tax Administration.`
> — `ADMIN/step-3-configure-the-service-14c3ef13.md`

A crawler resolving nav labels must accept both `Invoice` and `Invoice Admin` for the same menu entry.

**2. `Expense & Invoice Settings` is a FALSE FRIEND — do not map it to Invoice Settings.** In Professional Edition it is a *section of the User Details page* under User Administration, not an admin config page:
> `Employee Fields: Used by the Expense and Invoice Settings section of the User Details page.`
> — `ADMIN/fields-overview-5e3daf7c.md`
> `The User Admin may do the same on behalf of the employee using Administration  Company Administration  User Administration (Search & Select)  Expense and Invoice Settings  Approvers.`
> — `ADMIN/assigning-the-approver-for-the-purchase-request-user-20294611.md`

The one topic that treats it as a top-level menu is explicitly the **Standard Edition** surface (`Product Settings` / `View Advanced Settings` tiles), filed inside the Professional deliverable:
> `1.  Navigate to Administration > Invoice Settings or Expense & Invoice Settings.`
> — `ADMIN/standard-edition-d252f36e.md` (title: `Standard Edition`)

Two further Standard-Edition-shaped paths exist and should be excluded from the Professional taxonomy: `Click Administration > Expense & Invoice Settings \> Invoice Settings > Invoice Compliance.` (`ADMIN/accessing-invoice-pay-related-settings-4b605020.md`) and `Click Invoice > Invoice Settings.` (`ADMIN/accessing-invoice-pay-related-settings-bccf120b.md`). Both are Invoice Pay–specific and contradict the three consistent Professional Edition paths above.

**3. No page has been renamed or absorbed.** All three names — `Policies`, `Group Configurations`, `Invoice Settings` — are current and stable in 2026_08. The only rename recorded anywhere in the Policies guide history is a field-level one, not a page one: `Renamed the Authorization Request check box to Request on the guide's title page` (`ADMIN/policies-8b34cecf.md`). A separate historical note across many guides — `Tool now available from within Invoice Admin user interface.` — records the *relocation* of these tools into the Invoice Admin UI, which is what produced the `Invoice Processing Admin` left-menu structure.

**4. Whitespace hazard for verbatim matching.** In the two canonical "accessing" topics the `>` separator is rendered as U+00A0 non-breaking spaces (`Select Administration\u00a0 \u00a0Invoice.`). Any exact-string matcher over this corpus must normalize NBSP, or it will miss the highest-signal nav sentences in the set.

grounding: Verified all 31 candidates against the on-disk corpus at /mnt/c/Users/manci/PROJECTS/concur-corpus/CONCUR_INVOICE. 29 kept, 2 dropped.

METHOD: resolved every sourceFile path, then substring-tested each sourceQuote against the full file body (exact match plus a whitespace-normalized fallback) via a Python check rather than line-based grep, so a quote spanning a wrapped line could not produce a false negative. Then read all 11 cited primary files in full and spot-verified 21 additional corroborating quotes embedded in the notes fields.

RESULT: 30 of 31 cited files exist. Of those 30, all 30 sourceQuotes are EXACT verbatim substrings — no near-matches, no reworded quotes, no stitched fragments. That is an unusually clean extraction. No CSS selectors, DOM ids, or XPaths anywhere. No tenant-specific or BestRun-sandbox configured values: the doc-example strings present in the source files (Global / United States / Europe group names, Eastern Division and eastern1invoicecapture@concur.com aliases, the e-Bunsho and No Shows / This Employee system values) are all SAP-published examples or SAP system constants, and the extractor correctly kept them out of validValues.

DROP 1 — "Global" (the 31st entry): sourceFile is a non-existent path the candidate itself labels PLACEHOLDER. Pure duplicate of the kept "Global (Select Group hierarchy list)" entry, which cites the real tools-guides path. Fails check 1.

DROP 2 — "Invoice tab": grounding is sound (file exists, quote exact), but validValues lists seven group-aware FEATURE AREAS (policies, audit rules, payment types, car configurations, receipt limits, payment hold configurations, email reminders) rather than values the control accepts — a distinction the candidate's own notes concede. Rule 6 asks for accepted options; a runtime consumer would misread these as selectable. Failed closed. TWO NON-BLOCKING FLAGS for the graph owner. (1) The notes citation on "Global (Select Group hierarchy list)" to definitions-3e4ddcaf.md is lowercased ("a Named Vendor Group") where the file reads "A Named Vendor Group" — case-only drift in a supporting note; the sourceQuote itself is exact. (2) "Attendee Types" is typed as multiselect, but the corpus consistently describes it as a grid column with a per-row Modify link that opens a check-box window — a modeling nuance, not a grounding defect, and the companion "attendee type active check boxes" entry already captures the check boxes correctly.

The claimed label-drift pairs all check out against the corpus and are worth preserving for a runtime matcher: Attendee List Form vs Forms Fields; plural vs singular "Allow user(s) to upload CFDi attachments"; the historical "Allow Invoice Owners in Group to Create Payment Requests"; "Is Active for Group" vs "Is Active For Group"; and the three page-name variants Group Configurations page / Group Configuration page / Group Configurations List page. | refuter: Re-read all 30 existing cited files in full and machine-verified every sourceQuote as an exact substring (script over all 31 candidates). - Fabricated validValues (rule 6): "Invoice tab" — its seven "values" are the prose list of features the tab configures ("policies, audit rules, payment types, car configurations…"), which the entry itself concedes are "not data values"; fieldType "table" for a tab is also invented. - Quote does not support the field (nearby text): "Attendee Types" cites the parent/child inheritance NOTE, which never mentions this page or the column — the supporting sentence exists in the same file and was not used. "Group (list column)" is sourced from a conceptual topic about Editable By Groups / Applies to Groups, whose own text puts those columns on the Policies List page; the Group-column mention is incidental prose.
- Prose noun misread as a control: "Payment Types" — the quote says "…you must edit the policies and payment types…" in lower-case running prose; no file in the corpus ever writes it as a column or field label, unlike Policies and Attendee Types, which are both quoted as "in the … column".
- Value misread as a field: "Global" — the cited definitions file calls Global a Named Vendor Group ("such as Global (system created)"), i.e. a node in the hierarchy picker, not a control labelled Global.
- Invented label / duplicate node: "vendor group name" (corpus gives no label; almost certainly the Vendor Access instance of the already-captured Group Name). "Forms Fields (attendee form selector)" (concedes it is the same control as Attendee List Form, and "Forms Fields" is the name of a TAB on the different Forms and Fields admin page in that very file — active mis-resolution risk). "row selection check boxes" (generic grid affordance, sets no configuration state, fully subsumed by Delete Selected Rows / Select All / In Use).

dependencies.condition: Reframed from a candidate that attributed the source to Audit Rules, which the quote does not name. A row flagged In Use is referenced elsewhere in the configuration, has no selection check box, and cannot be deleted until the referencing configuration is changed.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In Use is an indicator that a group configuration is directly referred to within the overall configuration, and therefore cannot be deleted until that related configuration is updated.

dependencies.condition: Deleting a group configuration does not orphan its employees - they immediately fall back to the nearest ancestor group with a corresponding policy, up to the Global Group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Once a group configuration is deleted, the employees contained within the deleted group will now inherit the policies of whatever group above has a corresponding policy in place, all the way up to the Global Group if required.

dependencies.condition: Reframed to keep both endpoints on the audited page. Delete Selected Rows removes only the configuration, never the group - groups originate from the imported source list and must be removed there.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself.

dependencies.sourceField: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
dependencies.targetField: CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu
dependencies.condition: Cleared by default. Enabling the group-level check box exposes the CFDi Attachment command to users in that group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this setting (cleared/disabled by default) to allow users to view the CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu and attach a digital invoice image to their invoice.

dependencies.sourceField: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
dependencies.targetField: Attach CFDi and Delete CFDi menu commands
dependencies.condition: Verification trap: even after the group setting is saved the commands do not render on an already-open invoice until the user saves and reopens it. Their absence is not proof the setting failed.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Users will not see the Attach CFDi and Delete CFDi menu commands until they have first saved and reopened their invoice.

dependencies.sourceField: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
dependencies.condition: The group-level per-role selector is what puts the Vendor Banking Information section on the Request New Vendor page at all.
dependencies.sourceQuote: An option in the Group Configuration tool adds the Vendor Banking Information section to the Request New Vendor page.

dependencies.sourceField: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
dependencies.condition: Value semantics, distinct from mere section presence: Required blocks submission for approval until banking data is entered; Optional leaves it discretionary; Hidden removes the section.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If visibility is set to Required, the Invoice Vendor Manager will be required to fill in some banking information before submitting a new vendor for approval.

dependencies.targetField: Payment Request Attendee Detail View form
dependencies.condition: The per-group selection determines which Payment Request Attendee Detail View is rendered when a group member adds an attendee. LABEL DRIFT: this procedure calls the control the 'Forms Fields list', reached via Group Configurations > select group > Modify.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The selection that you have made determines which Attendee form that should be displayed when a new attendee is added.

dependencies.sourceField: Invoice Configuration administrator role group scope
dependencies.condition: Which groups are visible and editable on Group Configurations is set outside the page, by the group(s) attached to the Invoice Configuration administrator role. Rights cascade downward only. Quote contains a U+2019 apostrophe in 'administrator's'.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The administrator’s group access rights are defined in User Permissions when assigning the Invoice Configuration administrator role. They will have rights for the group defined and any group below it.

dependencies.sourceField: Invoice Configuration administrator role group scope
dependencies.condition: New group configurations can only be created for the administrator's own group and groups beneath it - never for peer or parent groups.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You can only create group configurations for groups for which you are assigned rights and for groups below those groups.

dependencies.condition: The group is chosen first and the PO configuration is built against it, so the group configuration must already exist.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration.

dependencies.condition: Silent fallback distinct from the ordering rule above: a group left without its own PO configuration uses the Global Group configuration, so a missing configuration is not a missing behaviour.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default.

dependencies.condition: Hard cardinality: one Invoice delegate configuration per group. Broader coverage must come from hierarchy inheritance, not from additional configurations.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Each group within your company can only have one Invoice delegate configuration. However, through inheritance a configuration created for one group can be applied to all the groups below it in the hierarchy.

dependencies.condition: Applies to the named vendor groups created on the Vendor Access tab. With no named group anywhere on the user's hierarchy path, the system does not restrict at all - the user sees every vendor at the Global level.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If no named group is defined in hierarchy path, then the user will have access to all vendors at the Global level.

dependencies.sourceField: source list levels and feature hierarchy
dependencies.condition: Named vendor groups created on the Vendor Access tab must match the source list levels built in Step 1 and mapped to the feature hierarchy in Step 2 - the names are not free choice.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.

dependencies.condition: Target retargeted to the field the quote literally names. The Vendor Access functionality does not appear in Group Configurations until Enable Vendor Segregation is set to Yes in Capture Processing Admin > Other Settings.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Now, the functionality appears in Group Configuration > Vendor Access

dependencies.condition: Ordering comes from the numbered configuration sequence in this file: Step 3 creates the alias and its child email addresses in Capture Processing Admin > Email Administration, Step 4 assigns that alias to a vendor group on the Vendor Access tab.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Step 4: Using Group Configurations > Vendor Access, assign a vendor group its email alias.

dependencies.sourceField: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
dependencies.condition: Configure the duplicate-check fields on Invoice Settings FIRST, then create the Is Duplicate rule in Audit Rules. Setting the fields alone does nothing - duplicate detection never runs until the audit rule exists.
dependencies.sourceQuote: After activating this feature, the admin must also create an Is Duplicate rule in the Audit Rules tool.

dependencies.sourceField: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
dependencies.condition: Direction corrected to match the graph convention (source controls target). If more than one field is selected on Invoice Settings, the Audit Rules rule must join them with an AND statement, or the multi-field selection is not honoured.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To use more than one option, admins will need to use an AND statement when creating the Is Duplicate audit rule.

dependencies.sourceField: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
dependencies.condition: Firing is conjunctive, not disjunctive: every option selected on Invoice Settings must match before the exception is raised. Selecting MORE fields makes the rule fire LESS often - the opposite of the intuitive reading.
dependencies.sourceQuote: All selected options must match for the audit rule to trigger

dependencies.sourceField: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
dependencies.condition: Enabled by default. Disabling it removes the Banking Import link AND all import/export functionality from the Invoice Payment Manager role, with no error shown - the link is simply absent.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If you disable the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information option, the Banking Import link and all the import and export functionality are no longer available for the Invoice Payment Manager role.

dependencies.sourceField: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
dependencies.condition: Distinct from the import-link effect: to force banking changes through the ERP / Vendor Master List instead of on-demand, the Invoice Processing Admin must clear this option first. The Payment Manager lockdown is the consequence, not a separate control.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Your company can turn off the ability to update banking details on-demand in Payment Manager. To do this, Invoice Processing Admins must clear (disable) the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information option in Invoice Settings.

dependencies.sourceField: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
dependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. No remittance email is ever sent unless this check box is selected; default is cleared in Professional Edition.
dependencies.sourceQuote: For vendors to receive these emails, you must select the Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types option on the Invoice Settings page.

dependencies.sourceField: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
dependencies.condition: The setting only produces mail if the vendor record carries an address in the Vendor Contact field of the Approved Vendor Import; only one address is supported. Enabling the toggle against an empty Vendor Contact yields silence.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The email address for notifications is determined by what is entered in the Vendor Contact field of the Approved Vendor Import.

dependencies.sourceField: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
dependencies.condition: Scope limit: the toggle only covers payments made through Invoice Pay. Client Pay payments never fire a notification however the setting is configured.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Payment of invoices that occur outside of Invoice Pay (Client Pay) do not trigger email notifications.

dependencies.sourceField: Peppol Integration feature activation by SAP Concur staff
dependencies.condition: OUT-OF-BAND PREREQUISITE, not a control on this or any page - it is a support service request. The Enable Peppol Integration check box does not exist for the tenant until SAP Concur staff turn the feature on, so a crawler finding it absent has not found it disabled.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Peppol Integration feature for Concur Invoice must be enabled by SAP Concur staff. Clients must initiate a service request with SAP Concur support.

dependencies.condition: The Invoice Settings check box (default cleared) only allows Peppol Integration; the actual field-level configuration is then done separately on the Peppol Configuration page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box to allow Peppol Integration and configure the feature in Concur Invoice.

dependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. CROSS-MODULE VALUE CONSTRAINT: once Peppol Integration is in use, Ledger Name on the Accounting Structure tab is pinned to the literal value 'Default'.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Customers using Peppol Integration must always set the Ledger Name as "Default".

dependencies.sourceField: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
dependencies.targetField: image deletion by the Invoice User
dependencies.condition: Selected (enabled) by default. Clearing it denies the Invoice User role the ability to delete an image from an invoice that was created for them by the AP User.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Invoice Admin can deny the Invoice User role the ability to delete an image from an invoice created for them. By default, the user can delete the image.

dependencies.sourceField: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
dependencies.condition: Selected (enabled) by default. The restriction is workflow-state scoped, not blanket: clearing it blocks the Processor from changing the vendor only while the invoice is pending ANY Processor role in workflow.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review).

dependencies.condition: Override layer 1: the site-wide default is a fallback only, applying to an invoice solely when no payment term is set on the vendor record.
dependencies.sourceQuote: With the Default Payment Term (days) option in Concur Invoice, you can specify default payment terms, which are used any time individual payment terms are not specified on the vendor record.

dependencies.targetField: per-invoice or Invoice Pay payment term
dependencies.condition: Override layer 2, distinct from the vendor-record layer: a term specified within the invoice itself or through Invoice Pay supersedes the Invoice Settings default. Default value is zero (0) days.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This amount is the default for all invoices unless a different number of days is specified either within the invoice or through Invoice Pay.

dependencies.sourceField: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
dependencies.condition: Value = From the associated purchase order line (the default): PO allocation lines and their field values are copied to the matching invoice line automatically.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the associated purchase order line option, PO allocations lines will automatically be copied down from the PO line to the associated invoice line.

dependencies.sourceField: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
dependencies.condition: Value = From the copy-down configurations: this field defers entirely to the copydown configuration built in Forms and Fields, which then governs BOTH PO-based and non-PO-based invoices. Choosing this value with no copydown configuration in place produces no copy-down at all. Spelling drift: rendered 'From the copydown configurations' in one topic.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the copy-down configurations option, the copydown configuration of allocation fields will apply to both PO-based and non-PO based invoices.

dependencies.sourceField: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
dependencies.condition: PRECEDENCE, distinct from the deferral rule above. Set to From the associated purchase order line, this Invoice Settings value overrides the Forms and Fields copydown configuration for PO-based invoices - so a Forms and Fields change will appear to have no effect.
dependencies.sourceQuote: With this setting, clients can copy down PO allocation lines regardless of the copydown configuration.

steps.name: Create a new invoice policy and make it selectable by a group
steps.goal: A new, correctly-formed invoice policy exists with its forms, workflow, image handling and expense types set, and members of at least one group can actually pick it when they create an invoice (it is Active for the group, with a default settled).

sequence.action: select the row of an existing policy to use as the base
sequence.rationale: There is no blank-form creation path in 2026_08: creation IS copying, so a base row must be selected before the Copy Policy button has anything to act on. SOURCE: "You can create a new policy by copying an existing one and changing the information as it applies to the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: click
sequence.rationale: This is what opens the editable New Policy page; every field below only exists after this click. Every dropdown also arrives pre-filled from the copied policy, which is why the following steps are edits, not first-time entries. SOURCE: "Select Copy Policy." and "The New Policy page appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: clear and type the new policy name
sequence.rationale: Rename first. The copy inherits the base policy's name, and every later corpus procedure addresses a policy as "the desired policy" on a list keyed by name — two same-named rows make Modify, Expense Types, Print Format and the Group Configurations assignment ambiguous. Ordering-within-the-page here is inference; the corpus only fixes Name as the first row of the field table. SOURCE: "Enter a name for the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the header form
sequence.rationale: A precondition outside this page, not an ordering choice on it: the option list is built elsewhere, so the form must already exist in Form Types before the writer arrives here. Selecting a name that has not been created yet is unrecoverable from this page. SOURCE: "You create Payment Request Header Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the line item form
sequence.rationale: Same external precondition as Header Form — the Line Item Form must pre-exist in Form Types. Grouped with the other form bindings because the corpus describes the policy as a container of exactly these four forms. SOURCE: "Select the Line Item Form to be associated with the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the allocation form (or deliberately leave it unset)
sequence.rationale: Must come BEFORE Allocation Separator, and this is a corpus-stated dependency, not a guess: designating an allocation form is what turns the allocation feature on, and the separator is dead until it is. Leaving this unset is a real decision — it disables allocation for the policy. SOURCE: "Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-). If the allocation feature is not activated (by designating an allocation form), the separator is not used." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: select the separator symbol
sequence.rationale: Sits after Allocation Form for the reason above: set before an allocation form exists and the value is inert, so a writer that sets it first cannot tell whether it took. Default is the hyphen, so skipping it is safe. SOURCE: "Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: select the vendor address form
sequence.rationale: Must precede the new-vendor-request toggle below, because that toggle exposes a request path that renders this form to the employee. Label on screen is Vendor Form; the object it names is a Vendor Address Form. SOURCE: "Select the Vendor Address Form to be associated with the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select Yes to permit employee-initiated vendor requests
sequence.rationale: Placed after both Vendor Form and Header Form because selecting Yes adds a link to the Create Payment Request Header page — the surfaces it depends on should already be bound. The corpus does not state this ordering; it is inference from the documented downstream effect. Note this is a Yes-valued selector, not a check box. SOURCE: "Select Yes to allow an employee to request a new vendor be added to the master vendor list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select or clear the check box
sequence.rationale: Order-independent within the General page — nothing else on the page reads it — so it belongs among the late General-page toggles rather than early where it would consume a decision the writer may not have an answer for yet. Label carries a trailing colon in the corpus. SOURCE: "Select this check box if you want to allow the Invoice User to have privileges to re-assign an invoice they have unassigned from themselves." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the workflow
sequence.rationale: Another pre-existence dependency outside this page: workflows are built in the Workflows area, so the target workflow must be published before the policy can point at it. Reuse is explicitly allowed, so a writer should not create a new workflow just because it is creating a new policy. SOURCE: "You create invoice workflows in the Workflows area of the Administrator." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md and "A workflow can be assigned to multiple policies." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/implementation-guidelines-for-policies-0c35d480.md

sequence.action: select the scan configuration, or knowingly leave it blank
sequence.rationale: Has no default, and the failure is silent: an unset value simply means scan never works for this policy, with no error to catch it later. The configuration must already exist on the Scan Configurations page in Image Handling, and one policy can hold only one. SOURCE: "Select a scan configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the scan functionality will not be active for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-assign-the-scan-configuration-to-a-policy-634c76ba.md

sequence.action: select the imaging configuration, or knowingly leave it blank
sequence.rationale: Same silent-failure shape as Scan Configuration, and it gates a visible downstream control (the View Image link for the Invoice Processor), so it must be decided here rather than discovered missing during processor testing. SOURCE: "Select an imaging configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the imaging functionality will not be active for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the owning group(s)
sequence.rationale: Set while still on the General page, because it decides who may reopen this policy at all — get it wrong and the writer can lock itself (or the intended group admin) out of every later Modify. The admin's own rights cap the choice, so Global may not be offerable. This is scope-to-EDIT only; it does not make the policy usable by anyone, which is why order 20 onward is mandatory. SOURCE: "Select the group(s) for which an administrator must have administration rights to modify the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: add the default billing address
sequence.rationale: Labelled Optional on this wizard, so it is safe to defer for a plain payment policy — but see step g1-s2: for a purchase-request policy the same field is required and blocks completion. A writer should treat 'Optional' as conditional, not absolute. SOURCE: "Add a default Bill To address to associate with new invoices." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: advance the wizard (Next) to the Expense Types for Policy step and read the copied rows
sequence.rationale: The General page must be complete before advancing, because the wizard does not return here on its own — later access is via the Modify button on the Policies list, a different entry point. The expense-type rows arrive copied from the base policy, so they are inherited state to audit, not a blank list. SOURCE: "The Expense Types for Policy step appears." and "This information is copied directly from the policy that you selected as the base for the new policy" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: read the per-row status before changing anything
sequence.rationale: This is the step most likely to be skipped and the most damaging to skip. Only Active expense types reach the employee's Expense Type list, and anything newly created lands Inactive — so a policy that looks finished can be unusable. Two values only: Active, Inactive. SOURCE: "All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive. For the system to use an expense type in a policy, the expense type must be marked as Active." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/expense-types-and-policies-a01e2537.md

sequence.action: multi-select the required expense types, then click
sequence.rationale: Acts on the current selection, so selection must precede the click — Shift+click / Ctrl+click builds the set in one pass, which matters because the button is applied per selection, not per row. Tolerate the label typo: one topic writes "Select Active or Deactivate." SOURCE: "Select the desired expense types and click Activate or Deactivate to change the policy status." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "Select the expense types to modify. You can select individual expense types or use Shift+click or Ctrl+click to select multiple expense types." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/change-the-status-of-an-expense-type-cf452b6a.md

sequence.action: advance to the Auto Submit Conditions step and add a condition row
sequence.rationale: Optional, and deliberately after expense types: auto-submit fires on import, so switching it on before the expense-type set is correct means the first imported invoices submit against a half-configured policy. The corpus does not enumerate the operators or operands in this editor, so a writer must be handed the condition, not guess it. SOURCE: "(Optional) If you would like to configure and use auto submit conditions, select Insert, and then enter the conditions that you want." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the check box inside the Auto Submit Conditions area
sequence.rationale: Only meaningful once a condition row exists (order 19), which is why it sits after Insert rather than beside it. It widens the trigger from import-only to assignment as well. SOURCE: "Auto-Submission Conditions: This option lets the administrator set basic conditions that, if met, cause the invoice to be automatically submitted by the system on import and optionally on assignment." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: advance to the Print Formats step and select the format, then commit the wizard
sequence.rationale: Last step of the wizard, and the terminal commit lives here — the corpus's final instruction is "Select Done.", which saves everything from orders 3-21 in one write, so abandoning the wizard earlier loses the whole policy. (No Done/Save control appears in the verified Policies field set, so it is named here in rationale rather than emitted as a field.) Default reports are conditional on being activated in this tool. SOURCE: "(Optional) If you want to configure and use print formats, select the print format that you want to use for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "NOTE: Any custom report that the admin creates will display for the user if the admin has activated the report in the Policies tool. Default reports are the only conditional reports." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/assign-a-print-format-to-a-policy-6bd703e7.md

sequence.action: on the group's row, click the Modify link in the Policies column
sequence.rationale: The hard page boundary of this outcome, stated outright by the corpus: creating the policy does not deploy it. Nothing an employee does changes until this sub-window is opened, and the Applies to / Editable By columns back on the Policies page are read-only reflections of what happens here. Cannot be done before order 21 — the policy row must exist in this list first. SOURCE: "Once you have created your policies, you must assign them to a group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/assign-a-policy-to-a-group-f9adaed6.md; corroborated "On the Group Configurations page, in the Policies column, select the Modify link for a list of policies available to the group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/change-the-active-policy-d656d79c.md

sequence.action: select the check box on the new policy's row
sequence.rationale: MUST precede Is Default Policy — this is an explicit corpus constraint, not an inference: an Inactive policy cannot be made the default, so a writer that reaches for the default column first simply finds it unavailable. This check box is also what makes the policy selectable at all. SOURCE: "If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: select or verify the check box in the Is Default Policy column
sequence.rationale: After activation, for the reason in order 23. Two traps a writer must expect rather than treat as failure: with exactly one Active policy the value is forced to Yes and cannot be set back to No, and with more than one Active policy a default MUST be nominated. SOURCE: "You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive. In addition, if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md; corroborated "If more than one policy is assigned to a group, then the administrator must specify one of the policies as the default policy (to be used if the employee does not select a policy)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/implementation-guidelines-for-policies-0c35d480.md

sequence.action: click to commit the policy sub-window
sequence.rationale: Terminal commit for orders 22-24; the sub-window's changes are not live until this returns to the list page. Only after this does the outcome hold end-to-end. SOURCE: "Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

steps.name: Stand up a PO / purchase-request policy with matching and receiving
steps.goal: A purchase-order-enabled policy (optionally purchase-request-enabled) exists with its PO forms, matching rule set and receiving switched on, its required billing address filled, and it is Active for a group so employees can raise purchase requests and PO-matched invoices.

sequence.action: select the existing Payment Request Policy row as the base
sequence.rationale: The corpus is unusually emphatic that the PR/PO policy must be derived from the existing default rather than built fresh — copying carries the working form and workflow bindings that a from-scratch attempt would have to reconstruct. SOURCE: "It is critical that the existing default policy be copied and then configured for PR/PO as described below. Select the Payment Request Policy, then click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: click
sequence.rationale: Same reason as the plain-policy flow: this is the only documented route to an editable new policy page. SOURCE: "Select the Payment Request Policy, then click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: rename the copy
sequence.rationale: The corpus names the rename as part of the copy instruction itself, not a later cleanup — a PO policy that still carries the payment policy's name is indistinguishable on the Policies list and in the Group Configurations policy grid, where the group assignment in orders 15-17 is made by name. SOURCE: "click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: select the check box
sequence.rationale: THE ordering fact for this whole step, and the corpus says it in so many words: this box is selected FIRST because every PO control below — the PO forms, PO Matching Ruleset, Enable Concur Receiving, and the Is Purchase Request Policy box itself — does not exist on the page until it is checked. A writer that tries to set PO Matching Ruleset before this will not find the control. It is also effectively one-way: it cannot be cleared once invoices exist under the policy. SOURCE: "Since the purchase request is associated to a purchase order, the Is PO Policy check box is first selected:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md; corroborated "Is PO Policy: Select this option to define the policy as PO-related. This selection causes the page to display additional options used under the PO policy and will ensure match rules run for any invoices associated with this policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md

sequence.action: select the check box (only if purchase requests are needed)
sequence.rationale: Second-level conditional: it is EXPOSED by order 4 and in turn reveals the Purchase Request Configuration group. Two conditionals deep means a writer must re-read the page after each check rather than assume a fixed field set. Skip this and you get a PO-matching policy but no purchase requests.
